50      The Savoy Male and Female College

    The "Diploma Course" advertised in the same catalog required the following subjects:
        Mental Philosophy, Moral Philosophy, Logic
        Rhetoric, Elocution
        Higher Arithmetic and University Algebra, Geometry, Trigonometry
        Ancient and Modern History
        Natural Philosophy, Chemistry, Physiology,
        Botany³²

    Although the schedule of this course by years and terms is not available, still the amount of time devoted to some of the subjects, as for instance the Mathematics, suggests the scheduling of similar subjects for the degree courses, the comprehensiveness of subject matter, and the amount of time required to complete the entire course. The "Higher Arithmetic and University Algebra" courses took their titles from the names of the respective texts, Robinson's Higher Arithmetic and Robinson's University Algebra, which together seem to account for a year's work in mathematics. Meteorology and Trigonometry accounted for at least another one-third year's work in mathematics. Similarly, under the Natural Science subjects, the textbook basis for the courses in Chemistry and in Physics may have determined the amount of work done on them. The original of the one of which a photograph appears was used in Savoy College and was priced at five dollars. The Art work included water color and oil painting and pencil sketching; instruction was, it can be estimated, from the scheduling for the degree course, at a half year each. A language course was probably available; but when violin instruction was offered there were very limited choices—Mr. J. D. Warren seems to have favored the violin (the "fiddle") as an instrument for young ladies.³³

³²Ibid., p. 10.
